verdict.rationale: Vercel documents some portability through standard interfaces. Functions can run any code from an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile. WebSocket handling works with standard libraries like `ws` 'with no additional configuration'. Storage moved away from proprietary Vercel KV/Postgres to standard external Redis/Postgres providers. However, the Build Output API is a Vercel-specific spec, and nothing shows code written against standard web runtime APIs running unmodified across multiple edge platforms. Missing for 10: documented support for standard (e.g., Web-standard) runtime APIs in edge/function code, explicit cross-platform portability claims, evidence that code runs unmodified on other edge platforms, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write code against standard runtime APIs so it runs unmodified across multiple edge platforms instead of being locked into proprietary storage/runtime APIs

citations.quote: Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
WebSockets in Vercel Functions work exactly like any distributed WebSocket server, so you can use libraries like ws to upgrade connections with no additional configuration
Vercel lets you connect external Redis databases through the Marketplace
